directiveSource: Explicit user instruction: adopt selective baseline-first process for all remaining cities
strategy: Breadth-first culturally significant experiences, then optional historical gap audits; stop exhaustive neighborhood-by-neighborhood searches.
scope: All remaining and revisited cities, not just Boston; restaurants, bars, pubs, theater, opera, music, museums, notable attractions and exceptional experiences.

include: Michelin stars/Bib Gourmand/Green Star and historically relevant Michelin selections
James Beard winners, finalists, notable semifinalists, distinguished chefs/bars
CAMRA recognized pubs and major brewing competition wins
Major arts and performance institutions, significant performances, culturally defining historic venues
Historically iconic or locally significant experiences
Notable hospitality/design awards, landmark cocktail bars, destination restaurants
Local reader recommendations and ordinary neighborhood taprooms only when exceptionally distinctive or needed to jog a known memory

interview.stopRule: Mark baseline complete after high-value candidates and one targeted historical-miss pass; do not demand exhaustive neighborhood coverage.

recordsPolicy.confirmedVisit: Create public visitor candidate regardless of awards; publication subject to separate explicit story review.
recordsPolicy.uncertainVisit: Private, not confirmed, never automatically published.
recordsPolicy.futureWishlist: Private and explicitly not visited; never public.
recordsPolicy.closedVenueInterest: Private historical interest only, not actionable future wishlist.
recordsPolicy.awards: Attribution must distinguish specific venue, chef, brewery brand, beer product, editorial list, community ratings, formal medals, and historical context.

alreadyAnsweredWishlistsExamples: Drastic Measures sister bar Wild Child

baselineRegions.result: 9 directly confirmed visits in final batch (8 preexisting canonical records, 1 newly added Officina), 2 private operating DC restaurant wishlists, Maydān maybe. No dates fabricated.

candidates.name: Lehua Restaurant at ʻImiloa
candidates.memoryCue: Lehua at ʻImiloa, Hilo; 600 ʻImiloa Place. Distinct from other Big Island places and unrelated to Maui.

candidates.name: ʻImiloa Astronomy Center
candidates.memoryCue: Planetarium and exhibits pairing Polynesian voyaging knowledge with Maunakea astronomy.

candidates.name: Lyman Museum and Mission House
candidates.memoryCue: Downtown museum and historic 1839 mission house; Hawaiian cultural and natural history.

candidates.name: Pacific Tsunami Museum
candidates.memoryCue: Downtown Hilo museum devoted to tsunami history, survivors and science.

candidates.name: Historic Palace Theater
candidates.memoryCue: 1925 Hilo movie palace hosting live theater, music, films and cultural events; building visit is not proof of a show.

candidates.name: Mokupāpapa Discovery Center
candidates.memoryCue: NOAA-led Northwest Hawaiian Islands culture and marine ecosystem exhibits, including large aquarium.

candidates.name: East Hawaiʻi Cultural Center
candidates.memoryCue: Gallery and events in Hilo's historic former courthouse/police station.

candidates.name: Hilo Farmers Market
candidates.memoryCue: Downtown open-air market for tropical produce, food, flowers and crafts.

candidates.name: Panaʻewa Rainforest Zoo & Gardens
candidates.memoryCue: Rainforest zoo and botanical setting outside central Hilo.

candidates.name: Wailuku River State Park / Rainbow Falls
candidates.memoryCue: Waiānuenue (Rainbow Falls) and nearby Boiling Pots viewpoints west of downtown Hilo.
